questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The central government has significantly reduced import duties on edible oils.
II. Edible oil prices in retail markets have dropped by nearly 15% over the past month.

Which of the following best describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both statements are independent causes producing a common effect
Both statements are effects of a common, unstated cause

questions.explanation: A is correct. Reducing import duty on edible oils lowers the cost for importers and traders, which gets passed on to consumers as lower retail prices. Statement I (policy action) directly leads to Statement II (market outcome). There is no reason to reverse this: falling retail prices do not cause the government to reduce duties. Option D is tempting — one might argue both follow from a 'global commodity price drop' — but the phrasing implies a direct domestic policy link.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The municipal corporation announced a strict ban on single-use plastic bags within city limits.
II. Several shop owners in the city have started stocking and selling cloth bags and paper bags.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are effects of the same independent cause — growing consumer awareness
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
The two statements are independent and unrelated

questions.explanation: C is correct. The ban on plastic bags (Statement I) creates demand for alternatives, prompting shop owners to stock cloth and paper bags (Statement II). The sequence is logical: regulatory action → market adaptation. Option B is a stretch — while consumer awareness exists, the more proximate and direct cause here is the ban. The statements are clearly linked, ruling out D.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The city's public bus service launched a new route connecting the industrial area to the central railway station.
II. Many factory workers have stopped using personal vehicles to commute to work.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both statements are independent causes of a common effect: reduced city traffic
Both are effects of an independent third cause: rising fuel prices

questions.explanation: A is correct. A new convenient bus route (Statement I) gives workers a viable public transport option, leading them to abandon personal vehicles (Statement II). The logical direction is: improved infrastructure → changed behaviour. Option B is reversed: workers giving up personal vehicles would not cause a bus route to be launched. Option D (fuel prices) is a possible independent cause but is not stated and the more direct link is between the two given statements.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. Rainfall this year was 40% below the long-term average in the major wheat-growing regions.
II. The government decided to import wheat from neighbouring countries to meet domestic demand.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are effects of the same independent cause — global wheat shortage
The two statements are unrelated
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect

questions.explanation: D is correct. Below-average rainfall in wheat-growing areas (Statement I) leads to lower domestic production, creating a supply shortage. To bridge this gap, the government imports wheat (Statement II). The causal chain is: drought → reduced harvest → import decision. Option B (global wheat shortage) is an additional possible cause but is neither stated nor required — the domestic drought alone is sufficient explanation.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The state government has increased the minimum wage for unorganised sector workers by 20%.
II. Many small businesses in the state have reported a rise in their production costs.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Both statements are independent causes of higher consumer prices
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are effects of an independent cause: higher inflation

questions.explanation: A is correct. A 20% minimum wage hike (Statement I) directly raises the wage component of production costs for businesses that employ unorganised workers (Statement II). The direction is unambiguous: policy action → business cost impact. Option C is reversed — rising production costs would motivate businesses to lobby against wage hikes, not cause the government to mandate them. Option D (inflation) could be a background context but is not the proximate cause stated.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. There have been frequent power cuts of 8–10 hours daily in rural areas of the district for the past three months.
II. Farmers in the district have shifted to diesel pump sets for irrigation.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Both are effects of an independent cause: rising electricity tariffs
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are independent causes of reduced agricultural output

questions.explanation: B is correct. Unreliable electricity supply (Statement I) makes electric pump sets unreliable for irrigation, prompting farmers to switch to diesel alternatives (Statement II). This is a pragmatic adaptation to an infrastructure failure. Option A (rising tariffs) might explain reduced usage but does not explain the complete shift to diesel — only prolonged outages would justify that investment. Option C is reversed: farmers using diesel does not cause power cuts.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. A prominent IT company announced the closure of its regional office in the city, displacing 2,000 employees.
II. Real estate developers in the city have reported a sharp decline in demand for residential apartments in the western zone.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both statements are independent effects of a global economic slowdown
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
The two statements are completely unrelated

questions.explanation: C is correct. The displacement of 2,000 employees (Statement I) reduces housing demand in the area near the office — many employees likely lived or were planning to buy homes in the western zone (Statement II). The causal chain: job loss / office closure → reduced purchasing power and need for local housing → lower apartment demand. Option B is plausible but too broad — the specific location link (western zone, where the IT office presumably was) ties Statement I directly to Statement II.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The state board of education has made attendance in remedial classes mandatory for students who scored below 40% in the annual examination.
II. Several schools in the state have reported a significant improvement in the pass percentage of weaker students over the past two years.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Both are effects of better teaching quality in government schools
Both statements are independent and unrelated

questions.explanation: B is correct. Mandating remedial classes for underperforming students (Statement I) is an educational intervention that, over time, leads to better academic outcomes (Statement II). The two-year period mentioned in Statement II is consistent with the lag expected for a policy to show measurable results. Option C (better teaching quality) is a plausible background factor but the specific mechanism described in Statement I is the stated intervention. Option A is reversed: improved pass rates don't cause mandatory remedial classes.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. The district administration conducted a mass sterilisation drive for stray animals last month.
II. Complaints about dog bites and animal menace in the district have reduced significantly this month.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Both are effects of an independent cause — increased public awareness about rabies
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are independent causes of better urban sanitation
Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect

questions.explanation: D is correct. A mass sterilisation drive reduces the stray animal population and, more importantly, calms the behaviour of treated animals — both contribute to fewer incidents of biting (Statement II). The temporal sequence is clear: the drive (last month) precedes the reduction in complaints (this month). Option A is weak — public awareness alone does not explain a sudden measurable drop in incidents within one month. Option B is logically reversed.

questions.stem:
Statements:
I. Domestic airlines have reported a 35% increase in passenger traffic compared to last year.
II. The government has approved the construction of a new terminal at the city's international airport.

Which of the following best describes the relationship?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is the effect
Both are effects of an independent cause: a post-pandemic travel rebound
Both statements are independent and unrelated

questions.explanation: A is correct. A sharp rise in passenger traffic (Statement I) puts pressure on existing airport infrastructure, prompting the government to approve a new terminal to handle the increased load (Statement II). The direction is: demand surge → infrastructure expansion. Option C (post-pandemic rebound) is a plausible independent cause of Statement I but does not directly explain Statement II — the government's construction approval is a response to the specific demand surge. Option B reverses causality: approving a terminal does not generate passenger traffic retroactively.
